title: Marseille and Strasbourg open Ligue 1 2026/27 in a clash of revamped teams
seoTitle: Marseille & Strasbourg kick off Ligue 1 2026/27 with.
subtitle: The French Championship's opening clash pits two clubs with significant squad and technical staff changes.
excerpt: Ligue 1 2026/27 kicks off with Marseille vs. Strasbourg. The opening match at Orange Vélodrome promises a clash of revamped teams and new faces.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The new season of the French Championship (Ligue 1 2026/27) kicks off this Friday, August 21, 2026, with a highly anticipated clash. Olympique de Marseille and Strasbourg will face each other in Marseille, at the legendary Orange Vélodrome Stadium, for the first round of the national tournament. The match, scheduled for 3:45 PM (Brasília time), will be broadcast by CazeTV.

Ligue 1 Kicks Off

The clash between Marseille and Strasbourg marks the beginning of the Ligue 1 2026/27 season. The match takes place at the Orange Vélodrome in Marseille, a venue known for hosting major French football games. The French Championship is one of Europe's most followed leagues, and its new edition begins with renewed expectations for several teams.

Olympique de Marseille and Its Transformations

Marseille starts the season at home, under the new technical command of Bruno Genesio. The coach's mission is to lead the club after the team finished last season in fifth place, securing a spot in the Europa League. The squad underwent a restructuring, with the departure of names like Mason Greenwood. On the other hand, Brazilian Igor Paixão has stood out offensively in the pre-season, scoring in the last four games. For the debut, Marseille will be without Quinten Timber, suspended due to accumulated cards.

Marseille's probable lineup is Jeffrey de Lange; Emerson, Leonardo Balerdi, Derek Cornelius, and Himad Abdelli; Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, Geoffrey Kondogbia, and Angel Gomes; Timothy Weah, Amine Harit, and Igor Paixão.

Strasbourg's Challenges in the Opening Match

Strasbourg also presents changes in its technical command, now under the leadership of Portuguese Hugo Oliveira. The team seeks to overcome a turbulent summer, which included the losses of midfielder Julio Enciso and full-back Valentin Barco in the transfer market. A significant absentee is striker Joaquin Panichelli, sidelined by a knee injury and not expected to return until 2027. The team relies on Sebastian Nanasi's creativity to try and break a taboo: Strasbourg has not beaten Marseille at the Orange Vélodrome since 1997. Strasbourg's away defense was a weak point last season, with only two clean sheets, the worst record in the division.

Strasbourg's probable lineup is Filip Jorgensen; Guéla Doué, Andrew Omobamidele, Ismael Doukouré, and Ben Chilwell; Pape Diong and Samir El Mourabet; Diego Moreira, Sebastian Nanasi, and Giovanni Reyna; Sékou Mara.

Recent History and Goal Expectations

The recent history between Marseille and Strasbourg points to balanced clashes with many goals. Five of the last six direct confrontations played at the Stade Vélodrome ended in a draw, with goals scored on all occasions. Of the last ten matches between the teams, six ended with an equal score.

Eight of the last direct encounters saw both teams find the net. Four of these eight matches also had over 2.5 goals, including both games last season (2-2 and 2-1). In the 2025/26 season, Marseille had ten home games that met this criterion, while Strasbourg, playing away, had eleven matches with the same outcome. With Mason Greenwood's departure, Marseille's offensive responsibility may fall on players like Amine Gouiri, who has a solid record against Strasbourg, with four goals scored in twelve matches. Last season, Gouiri registered a goal and an assist against this opponent in February 2026.

With information from LANCE!, Torcedores.
